prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct the GEOGRAPHY of this river-clearing woodcut while preserving its lovely printing style, palette, generous blank foreground and river shape.
The current picture wrongly puts the apple orchard and lean-to shelter on the FAR side of the river. In the story the player starts beside the orchard, builds their house, and only THEN builds a footbridge to cross toward the mill. Therefore move BOTH orchard and rudimentary shelter onto the NEAR bank, the SAME continuous ground as the large foreground clearing. The viewer must be able to walk from the blank foreground to both orchard and shelter WITHOUT crossing any water.
REMOVE all apple trees and the little lean-to from the far bank in the upper right. That far bank should be natural grasses, the existing two poplars and twin hills, no buildings or cultivated orchard.
ADD two or three rustic apple trees along the extreme RIGHT FOREGROUND margin, with their roots visibly BELOW the river on our bank, approximately x 88–98%, y 40–67%. Put the same crude three-pole thatch lean-to on the near bank at the upper-right edge of the clearing around x 84%, y 40%, BELOW the river's nearest shore, tucked among the near-bank trees. It is only an open lean-to, not a finished house. Use a bare-earth path along the RIGHT edge of the clearing to visibly connect it to the foreground. Do not insert a water channel between the player, orchard and lean-to.
Keep the large forked willow on the LEFT near bank. Keep the river crossing the upper third, and the consistent right-to-left current. Keep the central working space from x 12–78%, y 38–90% open, pale ochre and sparsely textured; no trees, structures or heavy hatching in this area. Do not shrink the usable play space. Broad irregular cuts, slightly misregistered ochre, slate-blue, rust and olive printing. No letters, labels, frames, icons or interface. Tall portrait same aspect ratio.
